items.title: 63520_Ernie Fields oral history interview
items.q: I ran across Louie shortly after that once... and he had Jack Teagarden on trombone; so I said Louie, that's something else, you took my man away from me and now it's you and Jack Teagarden.

ctx.x: So then a white trombone player came down, Dave Duncan, and he said I like your band, how come somebody else (inaudible). He

said he was down somewhere and wanted to join Jack Teagarden, but he had a small group and so he couldn't hire me and here you are, you're a trombone with a little group, so I guess you say you don't need me, and he said, let me tell you, I can do more than that. He said, I arrange and I can play piano. So I said, you're an arranger and he already was on me that he wanted to do something a little different, not just play, because I had already began to buy stocks--you know, arrangements, but I always like to have…

So I said, we could try to see what we could figure out, and he says, okay now, and he gave me his address. I didn't take him right then and he laughed, he said you're just trying to be nice and I said no, I'm going to try and figure out something. I got back into Tulsa and I had a call from Gladewater, Texas, they wanted bands down there, there's this big oil boom in east Texas then and wanted a band in Texas.
